thread.title: Dow Jones Down, Apple Weighs: Watch The Blue Chips | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Dow Jones Down, Apple Weighs: Watch The Blue Chips | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The Dow Jones industrial average, burdened by another 1%-plus decline by Apple ( AAPL ), showed a relatively mild decline in stocks today after a torrid start in 2019. The 30-stock blue chip average fell around 0.2% after rallying 2.4% last week. The Nasdaq did worse, with a drop of 0.6% after rising more than 3.4% last week for a third straight weekly gain.
X Large caps and small caps saw roughly the same size of decline. At around 3 p.m. ET, the S&P 500 and the Russell 2000 each lost 0.3% to 0.4%. Volume is running lower on both main exchanges Monday vs. the same time on Friday.
The Nasdaq 100-tracking PowerShares QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) fell nearly 0.9% for its second straight drop. However, QQQ has bounced off intraday lows. Ahead of the Q4 earnings season, it would take a 2% gain for the popular ETF to retake its 50-day moving average.
Meanwhile, the banking sector provided a nice counter-rally against the broad decline on Wall Street. Dow Jones industrial average components Goldman Sachs ( GS ) and JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) gained nearly 1% each on the heels of a favorable Q4 report by fellow Wall Street investment and commercial banking giant Citigroup ( C ). The stock now faces a clear test of resistance at the 50-day line, near 59.51.
Citi jumped more than 4% to 59.09 in heavy volume. The bank reported earnings that beat expectations, as revenue rose 9% . In a news release, Citi noted it bought back 74 million shares in the quarter, raising the total to 212 million shares for the year. The stock has 2.44 billion shares outstanding. Citi's operating costs fell 4% in Q4 vs. a year ago, "driven by lower compensation costs, efficiency savings and the wind-down of legacy assets."
A New Wave Of Earnings News Rolls In The fourth-quarter earnings season kicks into gear this week, as JPMorgan reports fourth-quarter results on Tuesday, followed by Bank of America ( BAC ), BlackRock ( BLK ), Charles Schwab ( SCHW ) and Bank of New York Mellon ( BK ) all on Wednesday. Please use the IBD Earnings Calendar to stay up to date.
The Street sees JPMorgan Chase reporting a 36% rise in Q4 earnings to $2.21 a share, according to William O'Neil + Co. data. That would stretch a three-quarter streak of double-digit EPS increases.
The banking titan has grown revenue 9%, 16%, 14% and 13% vs. year-ago levels in the past four quarters.
JPMorgan shares currently trade 15% below the 52-week peak of 119.24. No proper buy point has emerged for now. The stock has plenty of base-building activity to perform.
Beyond Dow Jones And Bank Stocks Lately, banks and financials have enjoyed a much-needed boost in January. Continued strength in this sector, plus software, retail and medical stocks, may provide additional stability to the big rebound after a waterfall decline in December across Wall Street.
Five Below ( FIVE ) is forming a new base . Shares dropped 2% to 115.16. But while the Philadelphia-based discount and variety chain is falling harder than the major indexes today, it's bullishly climbed back above the key 50-day moving average.
Lululemon ( LULU ), a former big winner during the 2018 uptrend, rallied sharply too. It has rejoined IBD Leaderboard as one of eight stocks in its watch list.
According to IBD Stock Checkup , the yogawear and athleisure clothing innovator boasts an excellent Composite Rating of 97 on a scale of 1 to 99. The IBD Composite Rating measures a stock's strength in fundamental, technical and institutional sponsorship factors.
Please read about Five Below and other companies that hit the IBD 50 Growth Stocks To Watch section to stay in touch with top stocks from the retail, tech, health care and other sectors of the market that could drive positive returns for growth stocks in 2019.
In Other Financial Markets Crude oil dipped 2% after rising sharply the past few weeks. U.S. near-term futures fell to a session low of $50.38 a barrel.
Gold futures edged up nearly 0.2% amid a major merger announcement by Newmont Mining ( NEM ) and Goldcorp ( GG ). The former agreed to buy its key rival in a $10 billion deal that would likely create the largest miner of gold and other precious metals.
